comparator.name: Industrial Engineering and Management
comparator.sourceNotes: The formally published 2026-2027 programme appendix establishes a complete 180-ECTS pathway: 60 ECTS of compulsory first-year courses; a 30-ECTS common IEM core across Years 2-3; a 40-ECTS specialisation; 30 ECTS of genuine minor space; and the 20-ECTS Bachelor Integration Project. The generic normalized target requires one of two equal 40-ECTS specialisations. Neither is formally presented as more representative, so Production Technology and Logistics is selected by the official-order tie-break. The minor space remains open rather than being populated with invented courses. Rechecked on 2026-10-14, the current programme page independently describes the degree as two-thirds technical science and one-third business, with training in mathematical and physical modelling, production, logistics, sustainability, management and technical/economic feasibility.

routeSelection.basis: The generic IEM target has two formally named, equal-sized specialisations and current official evidence does not establish either as more representative or general. The first-listed specialisation in the 2026-2027 appendix is therefore selected neutrally, without regard to UCR fit.

core: Industrial and organisational systems, process improvement and integrated technical-business decisions
Mathematics, programming, statistics, modelling, simulation and optimisation
Business economics, accounting, marketing, organisations, strategy and entrepreneurship
Production, logistics, supply chains, engineering design, manufacturing and quality control
adjacent: Sustainable production, renewable energy, lifecycle analysis and circular resource systems
Technology entrepreneurship, digital transformation and evidence-led product innovation
questions: How can models, data and optimisation improve industrial and organisational decisions?
How can innovation be evaluated and designed for technical, economic and environmental feasibility?

candidates.label: Sustainable production, energy and circular resources
Technology entrepreneurship and product design
candidates.reason: The completed closest programme already gives entrepreneurship, product design, strategy, market research and technical-economic assessment a substantial role. A third route would reorganise many of the same business and design courses rather than create a genuinely different 24-course curriculum.

selection.assessment: The closest related-fields programme addresses industrial decision-making through business, organisations, mathematics, data, optimisation and design while keeping the absent engineering spine explicit. The Sustainable Process Engineering and energy evidence supports one genuinely different environmental-technology route. Technology entrepreneurship and product design are already substantial parts of the closest programme, so a third programme would not add a defensible new educational choice.

alternatives.label: Industrial decisions, data & organisational systems
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines business, economics and organisational psychology with programming, data, statistics, optimisation, product design, strategy, governance and communication. The label does not claim industrial-engineering, logistics or manufacturing formation.
alternatives.concept: Combine business economics, finance, organisations and innovation with programming, data, statistics, optimisation and product design to study evidence-based industrial and organisational decisions. This is a related-fields response; it does not reproduce Groningen’s engineering-science, production, logistics, manufacturing or control sequence.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and nine level-300 courses. Business, programming, data, mathematics and research foundations precede organisational psychology, strategy, optimisation, algorithms, governance, econometrics, market research and deep learning; every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort term.

alternatives.label: Sustainable production, energy & circular resources
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum is centred on lifecycle analysis, resource recovery, environmental systems, renewable-energy design and sustainability governance, supported by mathematics, data, business, product design and stakeholder communication. It does not claim chemical-process or manufacturing engineering.
alternatives.concept: Study sustainable industrial questions through lifecycle analysis, circular resources, water–mineral systems, climate and renewable-energy design, combined with mathematical modelling, data, business foundations and product development. This related route addresses the Sustainable Process Engineering evidence without claiming reactor, separation, transport-phenomena or plant-design training.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and seven level-300 courses. Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II and the advanced resource and energy courses; Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra, numerical methods and probability; every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned Fall 2026 cohort term.
alternatives.distinctness: Fourteen courses, or 105 EC, differ in each direction. The second programme replaces advanced organisational, economics, marketing, communication, database, machine-learning, deep-learning, algorithm and optimisation study with lifecycle analysis, Earth-system tools, soils and aquifers, biogeochemistry, recovery, resources, renewable-system design and sustainability governance. These are curricular consequences of the sustainable-process and energy evidence, not threshold-filling substitutions.

notes.text: The UCR programmes develop quantitative decision-making, business and organisational analysis, product innovation, lifecycle assessment, circular resources and renewable-energy systems. They do not reproduce mechanics, materials and transport phenomena, manufacturing and CAD, physical system dynamics and control, production planning and quality control, mechanical craftsmanship or the 20-EC industrial integration project.

blocks: Both teach programming for modelling and problem-solving; UCR is general Python and computational reasoning rather than an industrial simulation sequence.
Both provide calculus and mathematical modelling foundations; UCR combines calculus with matrices, complex numbers and differential equations.
Both directly study linear algebra, matrices, vector spaces and transformations.
Both develop probability and statistics; UCR is a general mathematical course rather than industrial stochastic modelling.
Both address optimisation and constraint problems; UCR does so through AI search and optimisation rather than a full industrial operations-research sequence.
Both develop accounting and financial interpretation for business decisions.
Both study organisational behaviour, motivation, leadership and group dynamics.
Both use design processes for products and complex problems; UCR is consumer-product design and prototyping, not engineering-system construction.
Both address innovation strategy and implementation; UCR emphasises digital transformation and responsible value creation.
Both examine market evidence and customer response; UCR focuses on market research rather than industrial marketing as a complete field.
UCR introduces physics, chemistry and materials foundations for sustainability, but not the external course’s materials-and-molecules depth.
